content.value_statement: Developers need practical Azure Maps guidance without searching across SDK docs. This skill organizes .NET examples for geocoding, routing, map rendering, geolocation, and weather.
actual_capabilities: Explains package installation for Azure Maps search, routing, rendering, geolocation, weather, and resource management.
Shows authentication patterns using subscription keys, Microsoft Entra ID, and shared access signatures.
Provides .NET examples for geocoding, reverse geocoding, batch geocoding, and boundary polygons.
Covers routing workflows for directions, route matrices, route ranges, and traffic-aware options.
Includes examples for map tiles, IP geolocation, current weather, and SDK error handling.
limitations: Does not execute Azure Maps requests or validate user credentials.
Requires an Azure Maps account and valid authentication configured by the user.
Uses SDK versions shown in the skill file and may need review for newer releases.
Focuses on .NET usage and does not cover JavaScript or REST API implementations.

use_cases.title: Add Address Search
use_cases.description: Implement geocoding and reverse geocoding in a .NET application using Azure Maps Search clients.

use_cases.title: Plan Routes
use_cases.description: Create route directions, route matrices, and reachable range calculations for logistics or field service software.

use_cases.title: Render Location Context
use_cases.description: Fetch map tiles, country codes, and weather information for location-aware dashboards and internal tools.

prompt_templates.title: Start With Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to configure Azure Maps authentication in a .NET service using Microsoft Entra ID.

prompt_templates.title: Add Geocoding
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add address geocoding and reverse geocoding to an ASP.NET Core application with Azure Maps Search.

prompt_templates.title: Design Routing Logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a .NET routing workflow that calculates directions, traffic-aware travel time, and a route matrix.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Maps .NET design for authentication, rate limits, caching, error handling, and SDK package choices.

output_examples.input: I need to convert customer addresses into coordinates in a .NET service.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step plan covering package selection, client creation, request structure, result handling, and confidence checks.

output_examples.input: I need travel times between several depots and destinations.
output_examples.output: A routing approach that compares immediate and asynchronous route matrix options and explains when each fits.

output_examples.input: I need map imagery and weather context for a dashboard.
output_examples.output: A workflow that combines rendering clients, tile selection, weather calls, caching guidance, and error handling notes.

best_practices: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID for production authentication and keep keys outside source control.
Cache stable geocoding and map tile results to reduce cost and rate limit pressure.
Handle request failures, authentication errors, and rate limits with clear retry behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode subscription keys, client IDs, or SAS tokens in application source code.
Do not call batch routing or geocoding for every page load without caching.
Do not ignore confidence scores, address ambiguity, or regional differences in geocoding results.

faq.question: Which Azure Maps SDK areas does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers search, routing, rendering, geolocation, weather, resource management, authentication, and basic error handling for .NET.

faq.question: Does this skill make live Azure Maps calls?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users must run code in their own Azure environment.

faq.question: Can I use subscription keys with these examples?
faq.answer: Yes, but the skill recommends Microsoft Entra ID for production authentication when possible.

faq.question: Does it support batch geocoding and route matrices?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes batch geocoding, immediate route matrix, asynchronous route matrix, and route range workflows.

faq.question: Is this only for web applications?
faq.answer: No. The .NET examples can support services, desktop tools, background workers, and internal dashboards.

faq.question: What should I verify before production use?
faq.answer: Verify package versions, pricing, rate limits, regional availability, authentication policy, and caching requirements.
